query: Earlier efforts have produced HfNbTiVAl10 with a hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations and have used thermophysical-parameter calculations, CALPHAD, first-principles calculations, and machine-learning modeling to identify promising alloys. However, large computational demands and low efficiency impede rapid discovery, while fracture properties such as toughness remain difficult to predict. For HfNbTiVAl10 in its reported hierarchical-heterostructured state, what single testable methodological hypothesis could overcome these limitations for predicting Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness under tensile and fracture testing? Explain the rationale, quantify the expected gains in accuracy and efficiency over prior methods, specify the conditions under which it would cease to be reliable, identify supporting prior evidence, and define a blinded prospective benchmark that would decisively falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: For the hierarchically heterostructured high-entropy alloy HfNbTiVAl10, a two-tier ‘physics-aware’ multi-fidelity Gaussian-process surrogate that couples (i) inexpensive CALPHAD- and rule-of-mixtures–derived thermophysical descriptors (low fidelity) with (ii) a sparse set (≈15) of density-functional/experimental mechanical data points (high fidelity) and explicit microstructural length-scale descriptors can predict (a) Young’s modulus E, (b) 0.2 % yield strength σy, and (c) plane-strain fracture toughness KIC at 298 K and 10-3 s-1 with ≤5 %, ≤8 %, and ≤12 % mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), respectively, while reducing total CPU-time by ≥50× relative to conventional ‘DFT + CALPHAD + standalone ML’ workflows.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast Hf-22Nb-21Ti-22V-13Al (at %) alloy in the published hierarchical heterostructured condition: B2-matrix/BCC nano-lamellae with 20 – 200 nm platelets and multilevel chemical fluctuations; no post-casting heat treatment.
generation.intervention: Train a Bayesian multi-fidelity Gaussian-process regression model that combines (1) low-fidelity features (CALPHAD-predicted phase fractions, ΔHmix, Ω, δ, VEC, etc.) with (2) high-fidelity labels from a limited set of DFT elastic constants and experimentally measured E, σy, KIC, and (3) image-derived descriptors of heterostructure length scale and phase contrast obtained by automated TEM/EBSD analysis. Use active learning to choose the high-fidelity points.
generation.conditions: Predictions and validation experiments conducted at ambient temperature (298 ± 3 K), uniaxial tension at 10-3 s-1 on dog-bone specimens and fracture toughness on ASTM E399 compact-tension samples; compositions constrained to HfNbTiVAl10±3 at.% for any element; identical processing route as initial alloy.
generation.structural_mediator: Quantitative descriptors of hierarchical microstructure (lamellar spacing, phase-fraction variance, elemental partitioning amplitude) that mediate the link between chemistry/processing and mechanical response.
generation.mechanism: The Gaussian-process framework exploits correlations between low-cost thermodynamic/chemical descriptors and target properties, while Bayesian updating with a handful of high-fidelity points captures effects of lattice distortion and heterostructure-controlled dislocation and crack-tip mechanisms, yielding accurate uncertainty-aware predictions at orders-of-magnitude lower computational expense.
generation.predicted_outcome: MAPE: E ≤ 5 %, σy ≤ 8 %, KIC ≤ 12 % using ≤20 high-fidelity evaluations and <20 CPU-hours total; prior workflows require >1000 CPU-hours and give typical errors ≈10 %, 20 %, and 40 %, respectively—a ≥2× accuracy gain for E, ≥2.5× for σy, and ≥3× for KIC with ≥50× efficiency improvement.
generation.baseline: Conventional sequential CALPHAD+DFT databases fitted with random-forest/ANN models that treat chemistry only and ignore explicit multi-scale microstructure; reported errors ~10 % (E), ~20 % (σy), ~40 % (KIC); computation >1000 CPU-h per alloy search space.
generation.boundary: Reliability degrades if (i) composition deviates >±3 at.% per element, (ii) processing alters heterostructure (e.g., homogenisation or severe deformation), (iii) testing temperature departs >200 K from 298 K, or (iv) lamellar spacing falls outside 10–500 nm range, because the learned structure–property mappings no longer extrapolate.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate: success depends on sufficiency of microstructural descriptors and representativeness of the limited high-fidelity set; crack-tip plasticity/toughening mechanisms may introduce non-Gaussian noise not fully captured by the surrogate.

falsification_experiment.design: Blinded prospective benchmark: an independent team prepares 10 unseen alloy variants within HfNbTiVAl10±3 at.% using the same casting route and measures E, σy, KIC under the stated conditions. Prior to disclosure, the modelers receive only the chemistry, processing schedule, and microstructural descriptor set for each variant, plus permission to query low-fidelity CALPHAD outputs; they may request at most three new high-fidelity DFT or experimental points selected via active learning.
measurements: 0.2 % offset yield strength (σy) from tensile tests
Plane-strain fracture toughness (KIC) from compact-tension tests
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the averaged MAPE across the 10 samples exceeds 5 % for E, or 8 % for σy, or 12 % for KIC, OR if total computational cost exceeds 40 CPU-hours, the hypothesis is falsified.
